uncited: The method operates in two primary modes depending on the input: triangle-to-point expansion or direct point expansion.
Both modes rely on a geometry shader to generate cube geometry from a single input primitive.
Each triangle is processed to compute a centroid.
If the input is triangles, the vertex shader computes the centroid of the triangle and passes it to the geometry shader.
Receive vertices `gl_in[0]`, `gl_in[1]`, `gl_in[2]`.
The geometry shader receives either the computed centroid (from triangles) or the point data (from points).
For each of the 6 faces, check if the corresponding bit is set in `enabledFaces` and if the face is not culled.
If valid, call `AddQuad` with the appropriate offset and axis vectors.
If `(enabledFaces & 0x01)` and `!IsCulled(dx)`: Call `AddQuad(center + dx, dy, dz)`
If `(enabledFaces & 0x02)` and `!IsCulled(-dx)`: Call `AddQuad(center - dx, dz, dy)`
If `(enabledFaces & 0x04)` and `!IsCulled(dy)`: Call `AddQuad(center + dy, dz, dx)`
If `(enabledFaces & 0x08)` and `!IsCulled(-dy)`: Call `AddQuad(center - dy, dx, dz)`
If `(enabledFaces & 0x10)` and `!IsCulled(dz)`: Call `AddQuad(center + dz, dx, dy)`
If `(enabledFaces & 0x20)` and `!IsCulled(-dz)`: Call `AddQuad(center - dz, dy, dx)`
Define 4 corners `P0, P1, P2, P3` offset from `P` (centroid) by `±voxel_size/2.0`.
Compute vectors `V0 = P0 - P1` and `V1 = P2 - P1`.
Compute normal `N = normalize(cross(V1.xyz, V0.xyz))`.
Transform normal to view space: `v_normal = ModelViewMatrix * vec4(N, 0.0)`.
